name: Custom button made of div with onclick but no keyboard handler or tabindex
expectedCondition: All interactive functionality must be operable via keyboard interface.

name: Custom control with tabindex=0 but missing keyboard event listeners
expectedCondition: Focusable custom button must respond to Enter and Space keys.
failureCondition: Control receives focus via tabindex="0" but only listens to click event without keydown.

name: Interactive link with href omitted and no keyboard operation
expectedCondition: Anchor acting as link must have valid href to be keyboard focusable.
failureCondition: Anchor element has onclick but no href attribute and no tabindex.

name: Standard native HTML button accessible via keyboard

name: Custom ARIA button with keyboard handler for Enter and Space

name: Modal dialog opens without moving focus to dialog content
expectedCondition: When modal dialog opens, focus must move into dialog.

name: Modal dialog fails to restore focus to trigger element on close
expectedCondition: Closing modal must restore focus to the trigger control.
failureCondition: Focus is lost or resets to body tag upon dialog close.

verificationMethod: Manual inspection (Keyboard walkthrough, NVDA screen reader, DevTools accessibility inspector)

name: Positive tabindex disrupts logical sequential focus order
expectedCondition: Focusable elements must receive focus in an order preserving meaning and operability.
failureCondition: Element has tabindex="5" while surrounding elements have default (0), hijacking tab order.
verificationEvidence: Tab key jumps directly to field 3 before fields 1 and 2.

name: Modal dialog fails to trap focus allowing tab into background inert DOM

name: Compliant accessible modal dialog with focus management and restoration
expectedCondition: Focus moves into dialog upon open, is contained inside, and returns to trigger upon close.

name: Dynamic async status message injected into container without live region properties
expectedCondition: Status messages must be presented to assistive technologies via live regions without focus shift.

verificationMethod: Manual inspection (Keyboard walkthrough, NVDA screen reader, DevTools accessibility inspector)

name: Dynamic error message added without role=alert or aria-live=assertive
expectedCondition: Error status messages must be exposed as live regions.
failureCondition: Error text injected into non-live container; assistive technology not notified.
verificationEvidence: Screen reader does not announce validation error.
verificationMethod: Manual inspection (Keyboard walkthrough, NVDA screen reader, DevTools accessibility inspector)

name: Live region dynamically created at moment of message injection (race condition)
expectedCondition: Live region should exist in DOM prior to text injection so browser registers mutation listeners.
failureCondition: Live region container created simultaneously with text, often dropped by screen reader engines.
verificationEvidence: Screen readers frequently miss announcement when role="status" is injected along with text in one paint.
verificationMethod: Manual inspection (Keyboard walkthrough, NVDA screen reader, DevTools accessibility inspector)

name: Status message container has aria-live=off explicitly suppressing announcements
expectedCondition: Status message regions must allow announcements (polite or assertive).
failureCondition: Container has aria-live="off", explicitly muting status updates.
verificationEvidence: ARIA live property is computed as "off"; screen reader ignores text updates.
verificationMethod: Manual inspection (Keyboard walkthrough, NVDA screen reader, DevTools accessibility inspector)

name: Compliant status message using persistent role=status and aria-live=polite
expectedCondition: Status message is injected into existing polite live region, announcing without focus disruption.
failureCondition: None.
verificationEvidence: CDP Accessibility Tree reports role="status" and live="polite"; NVDA announces message automatically.
verificationMethod: Manual inspection (Keyboard walkthrough, NVDA screen reader, DevTools accessibility inspector)
